<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. II.|ACCORDING TO S. MARKE.|91}}</noinclude>passed by, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 9, 9. Lu. 5, 27.''}}* he savv Leui of Alphæus sitting at the custome place: and he saith to him, Folovv me. And rising vp he folovved him. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=15}}† And it came to passe, as he sate at meate in his house, many Publicans and sinners did sit dovvne together vvith {{sc|Iesvs}} and his Disciples. for they vvere many, vvho also folovved him. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=16}}† And the Scribes and the Pharisees seeing that he did eate vvith Publicans and Sinners, said to his Disciples, Why doth your Maister eate and drinke vvith Publicans and sinners? {{verse|chapter=2|verse=17}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} hearing this, saith to them, The vvhole haue not neede of a Physicion, but they that are il at ease. for I came not to call the iust, but sinners.

{{verse|chapter=2|verse=18}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 9, 13. Lu. 5, 33.''}}* the disciples of Iohn and the Pharisees did vse to fast: and they come, and say to him, Why do the disciples of Iohn and of the Pharisees fast: but thy disciples do not fast? {{verse|chapter=2|verse=19}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} said to them, Why, can the children of the mariage fast, as long as the bridegrome is vvith them? So long time as they haue the bridegrome vvith them, they can not fast. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=20}}† But the daies vvil come vvhen the bridegrome shal be taken avvay from them: and then they shal {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ He foretelleth that fasting shal be vsed in his Church, no lesse then in the old law or in the time of Iohn the Baptist. ''See Mat. c. 9, 15''.}}∷ fast in those daies. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=21}}† No body sovveth a peece of ravv cloth to an old garment: othervvise he taketh avvay the nevv peecing from the old, and there is made a greater rent. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=22}}† And no body putteth nevv vvine into old bottels: othervvise the vvine bursteth the bottels, and the vvine vvil be shed, and the bottels vvil be lost. but nevv vvine must be put into nevv bottels.

{{verse|chapter=2|verse=23}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 12, 1. Lu. 6, 1.''}}* it came to passe againe vvhen he vvalked through the corne on the Sabboths, and his Disciples began to goe forvvard and to plucke the eares. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=24}}† And the Pharisees said to him, Behold, vvhy do they on the Sabboths that vvhich is not lavvful? {{verse|chapter=2|verse=25}}† And he said to them, Did you neuer read vvhat Dauid did, vvhen he vvas {{sup|‖}} in necessitie, and him self vvas an hungred and they that vvere vvith him? {{verse|chapter=2|verse=26}}† hovv {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''1. Re. 21, 6.''}}* he entred into the house of God vnder Abiathar the high Priest, and did eate the loaues of Proposition, vvhich it vvas not lavvful to eate {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Leu. 24, 9.''}}* but for the Priests, and did giue vnto them vvhich vvere vvith him? {{verse|chapter=2|verse=27}}† And he said to them, The Sabboth vvas made for man, and not man for the Sabboth. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=28}}† Therfore the sonne of man is {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The maker of the law may abrogate or dispense whē and where for iust cause it seemeth good to him.}}∷ Lord of the Sabboth also.<noinclude>{{rh||M ij|ANNOT.}}</noinclude>
